topic: Trải nghiệm portop trên VPS Linux: "htop cho cổng mạng" giám sát Docker và tiến trình thay thế netstat và lsof

repos.name: portop
repos.description: htop for your ports. Inspect processes, Docker & systemd, detect port drift, audit Compose, and manage it all from TUI, Web or Cockpit.

notes.audience: Linux VPS administrators, self-hosters, and developers managing Docker containers and services who need an intuitive, real-time socket and port monitor.
notes.angle: Thay thế sự rườm rà của netstat hay lsof bằng giao diện TUI phong cách htop trực quan: hiển thị rõ process, container Docker/Podman, tình trạng tường lửa và hỗ trợ giải phóng port chỉ với một lệnh.

facts.fact: portop là công cụ giao diện dòng lệnh dạng TUI viết bằng Go (giấy phép MIT) dùng để theo dõi socket TCP và UDP trên hệ thống.
facts.quote: portop is an htop-style terminal UI for the TCP and UDP sockets on a machine.

facts.fact: Cung cấp bảng socket cập nhật trực tiếp theo thời gian thực kèm thông tin tiến trình, PID, mức dùng CPU, user và tên dịch vụ.
facts.quote: A live table of listening and established sockets with process, PID, CPU, user and service names (`:22 ssh`), sortable by any column.

facts.fact: Tự động nhận diện systemd unit, Windows service hoặc container Docker, Podman, Kubernetes gắn với từng socket thông qua cgroups mà không cần cài thêm daemon phụ.
facts.quote: The systemd unit or Windows service, and the Docker, Podman or Kubernetes container behind each socket, read from cgroups with no daemon of its own.

facts.fact: Gom nhóm các tiến trình máy chủ dạng master-worker (như Nginx, PHP-FPM, Apache) vào một dòng duy nhất để tránh rối mắt.
facts.quote: One row for a server's master and its workers: `nginx +3`.

facts.fact: Hiển thị lưu lượng mạng tức thời (bytes per second) cho từng kết nối TCP đang thiết lập trên Linux và macOS.
facts.quote: Bytes per second for every established TCP connection (Linux, macOS).

facts.fact: Mã hóa màu các cổng đang lắng nghe dựa theo phạm vi phơi nhiễm: toàn bộ interface (0.0.0.0), một IP cụ thể, hoặc chỉ loopback (127.0.0.1).
facts.quote: Listening ports colored by exposure: every interface, one address or loopback only.

facts.fact: Đọc cấu hình tường lửa của máy chủ (ufw, firewalld, nftables) để đưa ra đánh giá: cho phép kết nối (allowed), giới hạn nguồn (restricted) hoặc chặn (blocked).
facts.quote: The host firewall's verdict for exposed ports: allowed, restricted to some sources, or blocked.

facts.fact: Hỗ trợ gửi tín hiệu SIGTERM hoặc SIGKILL trực tiếp từ bàn phím để dừng tiến trình, có bước xác minh lại danh tính tiến trình trước khi ngắt.
facts.quote: Process details, and SIGTERM or SIGKILL after a confirmation that re-checks the process identity.

facts.fact: Cung cấp lệnh tự động hóa `--free <port>` để ngắt tiến trình đang chiếm dụng port và chờ cho đến khi port được giải phóng hoàn toàn.
facts.quote: `--free 3000` stops whatever holds a port and waits until it is released.

facts.fact: Hỗ trợ cờ `--wait <port>` giúp script tạm dừng cho tới khi có một service bắt đầu lắng nghe trên cổng chỉ định.
Khả năng lưu mốc chuẩn (baseline) và so sánh sai lệch (`--diff`) trả về mã thoát exit code 3 khi phát hiện port mới mở, port bị đóng hoặc đổi phạm vi lắng nghe.
facts.quote: `--save-baseline` and `--diff` (exit code 3) report ports that appear, disappear or become reachable from the network, from cron or CI.

facts.fact: Hỗ trợ kiểm tra dự án Docker Compose (`--compose DIR`) để đối chiếu giữa các port khai báo mở và các port thực tế đang lắng nghe.
facts.quote: `--compose DIR` checks a Docker Compose project's published ports against what actually listens.

facts.fact: Tích hợp sẵn giao diện Web dashboard hiển thị bảng socket và cho phép quản trị qua trình duyệt ở cổng mặc định 8088.
Trên các cụm Kubernetes (containerd/CRI-O), portop lấy tên namespace/pod/container trực tiếp qua đường dẫn log `/var/log/containers` mà không cần quyền API hay lệnh crictl.
facts.quote: The names come from the kubelet's log links in /var/log/containers, so no API access or crictl is needed; run portop on the node, usually with sudo.

facts.fact: Dữ liệu tường lửa được đọc lại tối đa mỗi 30 giây một lần và có thể tắt kiểm tra bằng cờ `--no-firewall`.
facts.quote: Rules are read at most every 30 seconds. Turn the check off with --no-firewall or resolve_firewall: false.

facts.fact: Web dashboard cung cấp endpoint `/metrics` định dạng Prometheus hỗ trợ giám sát trạng thái và số lượng listening ports.
facts.quote:
/metrics serves the Prometheus text format:

portop_sockets
protocol, state
portop_listening_ports
protocol, scope

facts.fact: Web dashboard bắt buộc phải bật xác thực (sign-in) mới cho phép lắng nghe ra ngoài địa chỉ loopback (remote access).
facts.quote: Only a dashboard with sign-in may listen beyond loopback:

facts.fact: Phiên đăng nhập trên web kéo dài 12 giờ và tự động khóa IP 1 phút nếu nhập sai mật khẩu 5 lần liên tiếp.
facts.quote: Sessions last 12 hours and end when portop stops. After five failed sign-ins a client, an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64, waits a minute.

caveats: Cần chạy dưới quyền `sudo` (hoặc Administrator) để xem được tiến trình của user khác và đọc trạng thái tường lửa; nếu chạy không có root, tường lửa sẽ hiển thị dấu `?`.
Trên Linux, nếu hệ thống áp dụng các rule nftables input phức tạp hoặc firewalld rich rules, portop không thể phân tích chính xác và sẽ hiển thị verdict là `?`.
Trên macOS và Windows chạy Docker Desktop qua máy ảo (VM), portop không thể nhìn thấy tiến trình bên trong container mà chỉ nhận biết qua các port được Docker publish ra host.
Việc truyền mật khẩu Web dashboard qua cờ `--web-password PASS` sẽ bị lộ trong bảng tiến trình (`ps`) cho các người dùng khác trên máy chủ; nên sử dụng biến môi trường `PORTOP_WEB_PASSWORD`.
Tường lửa được quét tối đa 30 giây một lần nên những thay đổi rule firewall tức thời sẽ có độ trễ trước khi cập nhật trên bảng TUI.
gaps: Mức tiêu hao tài nguyên CPU và RAM của portop khi chạy dashboard liên tục trên VPS cấu hình thấp (1 vCPU, 512MB–1GB RAM) là bao nhiêu?
Lệnh `portop --free` xử lý tiến trình bằng SIGTERM trước hay lập tức SIGKILL nếu tiến trình bị treo, và thời gian chờ (timeout) mặc định là bao lâu?
Khả năng mở rộng và hiệu năng hiển thị của bảng TUI khi máy chủ có hàng chục nghìn kết nối đồng thời (high-load proxy hoặc game server lớn) như thế nào?

## padovanl/portop (https://github.com/padovanl/portop)
Description: htop for your ports. Inspect processes, Docker & systemd, detect port drift, audit Compose, and manage it all from TUI, Web or Cockpit.
Homepage: https://padovanl.github.io/portop/
Language: Go; license: MIT; created 2026-08-15; last push 2026-11-07
Latest release: v0.4.0 (2026-11-07)
README (start):
# portop

[](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/actions/workflows/release.yml)
[](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/releases/latest)
[](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/releases)
[](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/padovanl/portop)
[](go.mod)
[](LICENSE)

[](https://snapcraft.io/portop)
[](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/portop)
[](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html#apt)
[](https://cli.masoko.net/tools/portop/)
[](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MZ319F4LW70)
[](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/pull/453604)

**[Website](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/) · [Documentation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/) · [Releases](https://github.com/padovanl/portop/releases)**

portop is an htop-style terminal UI for the TCP and UDP sockets on a machine.
For every port it shows the process, its systemd unit or Windows service, its
Docker, Podman or Kubernetes container, who can reach it and what the firewall
does with it, and it lets you inspect or stop the owner from the keyboard. It
runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, in the terminal, in a browser or inside
Cockpit.

## ✨ Features

**See what is using your ports**
- A live table of listening and established sockets with process, PID, CPU,
  user and service names (`:22 ssh`), sortable by any column.
- The systemd unit or Windows service, and the Docker, Podman or Kubernetes
  container behind each socket, read from cgroups with no daemon of its own.
- One row for a server's master and its workers: `nginx +3`.
- Bytes per second for every established TCP connection (Linux, macOS).

**Know who can reach them**
- Listening ports colored by exposure: every interface, one address or
  loopback only.
- The host firewall's verdict for exposed ports: allowed, restricted to some
  sources, or blocked.

**Act on them**
- Process details, and SIGTERM or SIGKILL after a confirmation that re-checks
  the process identity.
- `--wait 5432` blocks until a service listens; `--free 3000` stops whatever
  holds a port and waits until it is released.
- Open a port in the browser, copy a row, filter by any word.

**Catch changes**
- New listening ports are highlighted live, with an optional desktop
  notification.
- `--save-baseline` and `--diff` (exit code 3) report ports that appear,
  disappear or become reachable from the network, from cron or CI.
- `--compose DIR` checks a Docker Compose project's published ports against
  what actually listens.

**Use it anywhere**
- `--json` for scripts, a web dashboard with sign-in, TLS and Prometheus
  `/metrics`, and a Cockpit add-on.
- 13 themes and remappable keys from a live settings screen.

## 📥 Install

| System | Command |
|--------|---------|
| Debian, Ubuntu | [APT repository](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html#apt) |
| Linux (Snap) | `sudo snap install portop` |
| macOS, Linux | `brew install portop` |
| Windows | `winget install padovanl.portop`, or the [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MZ319F4LW70) |
| Linux, macOS | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/padovanl/portop/main/install.sh \| sh` |
| From source | `go install github.com/padovanl/portop/cmd/portop@latest` |

The APT repository serves amd64, arm64 and armhf:

```bash
sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://apt.lucapadovan.dev/lucapadovan.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/lucapadovan.gpg >/dev/null
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/lucapadovan.gpg] https://apt.lucapadovan.dev stable main" \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lucapadovan.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install portop
```

Release archives cover Linux on amd64, arm64, ARMv7 and ARMv6, macOS on Intel
and Apple Silicon, and Windows on x64 and ARM64, with `.deb` and `.rpm`
packages for Linux. See [Installation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html)
for every option.

## ⌨️ Usage

```bash
portop                      # the live table
portop nginx 443            # filtered: every word must match
portop --listen             # listening sockets only
portop --json               # one snapshot for scripts

portop --wait 5432          # exit 0 once something listens
portop --free 3000          # stop whatever holds the port

portop --save-baseline      # record what listens now
portop --diff               # exit 3 if that changed
portop --compose ./stack    # audit a Compose project's ports

portop --web                # dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8088
```

Run `sudo portop` (an Administrator terminal on Windows) to see other users'
processes and read the firewall. In the table, press `?` for help and `,` for
settings. The [documentation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/) covers
every flag, the JSON fields, exit codes and what each platform supports.

## 🆚 Why not just `ss -tlnp`?

|                                  | ss / netstat | lsof | bandwhich | portop |
|----------------------------------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Live, refreshing view            | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Owning process                   | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| systemd unit, Windows service    | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Docker, Podman, Kubernetes       | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Exposure and firewall verdict    | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Per-connection traffic           | ✅ `-ti` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Stop the owner, safely           | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| `--wait` / `--free` for scripts  | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Baseline drift, Compose audit    | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Web dashboard, Prometheus        | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Linux, macOS and Windows         | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |

## 📚 Documentation

- [Installation](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/installation.html) and [first run](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/first-run.html)
- [The table](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/the-table.html): columns, colors, keys
- [Command line](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/command-line.html) and [scripting](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/scripting.html)
- [Baseline drift](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/baseline.html) and [Compose audit](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/compose.html)
- [Containers](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/containers.html), [firewall](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/firewall.html) and [traffic](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/traffic.html)
- [Web dashboard and metrics](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/web-dashboard.html), [Cockpit add-on](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/cockpit.html)
- [Configuration](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/configuration.html) and [platform support](https://padovanl.github.io/portop/docs/platforms.html)

The documentation is generated from [`docs-src/`](docs-src) with
`python3 scripts/build-docs.py`; preview the whole site with
`python3 scripts/serve-pages.py`.

## 🤝 Contributing

Pull requests are welcome; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Open them
against `develop`, and run `gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test ./...` before
pushing.

## 📄 License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## wellsgz/portmon (https://github.com/wellsgz/portmon)
Description: Lightweight eBPF-based TCP port traffic monitor with real-time TUI dashboard
Homepage: -
Language: Go; license: none; created 2025-12-27; last push 2026-01-04
Latest release: v0.4.5 (2026-01-04)
README (start):
# eBPF Port Traffic Monitor

[](https://github.com/wellsgz/portmon/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://github.com/wellsgz/portmon/releases)
[](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

A lightweight, real-time network traffic monitoring tool using eBPF kprobes to monitor bidirectional TCP traffic on specified ports. Features persistent historical data storage and both CLI and TUI interfaces.

## Features

- 🚀 **eBPF-powered** - Minimal overhead using kernel-level packet tracing
- 📊 **Realtime + Historical** - Live stats and SQLite-backed historical data
- 🖥️ **TUI Dashboard** - Interactive terminal UI with date range selection
- 📝 **Port Descriptions** - Label ports in config for easy identification
- 💾 **Billing Cycle Support** - Custom date ranges for usage tracking
- 📦 **Debian Package** - Easy installation via `.deb` package
- 🔧 **Systemd Ready** - Includes service file for production deployment

## Requirements

- **Linux kernel 5.4+** with BTF support
- **Go 1.21+**
- **clang/llvm** and **libbpf-dev** (for eBPF compilation)
- Root privileges (for eBPF loading)

## Installation

### From Release (Debian Package)

```bash
# Download and install .deb (recommended)
curl -LO https://github.com/wellsgz/portmon/releases/latest/download/portmon_0.4.2_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i portmon_0.4.2_amd64.deb
```

### From Release (Tarball)

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/wellsgz/portmon/releases/latest/download/portmon-linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar -xzf portmon-linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo mv portmond portmon /usr/local/bin/
```

### From Source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/wellsgz/portmon.git
cd portmon

# Install dependencies
make deps

# Generate vmlinux.h and build
make vmlinux generate build
```

## Quick Start

```bash
# Start daemon (requires root)
sudo portmond --port 5000 --port 8080

# Launch TUI (another terminal)
portmon tui

# Or use CLI
portmon stats --port 5000
portmon stats --port 5000 --today
portmon stats --port 5000 --cycle-day 15  # Billing cycle
portmon status
```

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Daemon (portmond)                        │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌────────────┐               │
│  │  eBPF    │─▶│ Aggregator │─▶│ IPC Server │               │
│  │ Collector│  └─────┬──────┘  └──────┬─────┘               │
│  └──────────┘        │                │                     │
│                      ▼                │                     │
│               ┌──────────┐            │                     │
│               │ SQLite   │            │                     │
│               └──────────┘            │                     │
└───────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘
                                        │ Unix Socket
                                        ▼
                              ┌─────────────────┐
                              │ CLI/TUI Client  │
                              │   (portmon)     │
                              └─────────────────┘
```

## Configuration

### Config File (Recommended)

Create `/etc/portmon/portmon.yaml`:

```yaml
# Ports with descriptions (recommended)
ports:
  - port: 5000
    description: "API Server"
  - port: 8080
    description: "Web Frontend"

# Simple format also supported:
# ports:
#   - 5000
#   - 8080

data_dir: /var/lib/portmon
socket: /run/portmon/portmon.sock
retention_days: 90
log_level: info
```

Then run: `sudo portmond` or `sudo portmond -c /path/to/config.yaml`

### CLI Options

CLI flags override config file values:

```bash
portmond \
  --config /etc/portmon/portmon.yaml \
  --port 5000 \               # Ports to monitor (repeatable)
  --data-dir ~/.portmon \     # Data directory
  --retention-days 180 \      # Data retention (1-365 days)
  --socket ~/.portmon/portmon.sock \
  --log-level info            # debug, info, warn, error

# CLI options
portmon stats --port 5000 --today       # Today's stats
portmon stats --port 5000 --cycle-day 15  # Billing cycle (15th-14th)
portmon stats --port 5000 --json        # JSON output
```

## TUI Keybindings

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `q` | Quit |
| `d` | Change date range |
| `↑/↓` | Navigate ports |
| `r` | Force refresh (syncs Period Summary) |
| `?` | Help |

## Systemd Service

```bash
# Install service
sudo cp configs/portmond.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo cp configs/portmon.yaml.example /etc/portmon/portmon.yaml

# Edit config
sudo nano /etc/portmon/portmon.yaml

# Enable and start
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now portmond
```

## License

MIT

# bandwhich

This is a CLI utility for displaying current network utilization by process, connection and remote IP/hostname

## Table of contents

- [bandwhich](#bandwhich)
  - [Table of contents](#table-of-contents)
  - [Project status](#project-status)
  - [How does it work?](#how-does-it-work)
  - [Installation](#installation)
    - [Downstream packaging status](#downstream-packaging-status)

    - [1. `setcap`](#1-setcap)
      - [Capabilities explained](#capabilities-explained)

  - [Post install (Windows)](#post-install-windows)
  - [Usage](#usage)
  - [Contributing](#contributing)
  - [License](#license)

## Project status

This project is in passive maintenance. Critical issues will be addressed, but
no new features are being worked on. However, this is due to a lack of funding
and/or manpower more than anything else, so pull requests are more than welcome.
In addition, if you are able and willing to contribute to this project long-term,
we would like to invite you to apply for co-maintainership.

For more details, see [The Future of Bandwhich #275](https://github.com/imsnif/bandwhich/issues/275).

## How does it work?

`bandwhich` sniffs a given network interface and records IP packet size, cross referencing it with the `/proc` filesystem on linux, `lsof` on macOS, or using WinApi on windows. It is responsive to the terminal window size, displaying less info if there is no room for it. It will also attempt to resolve ips to their host name in the background using reverse DNS on a best effort basis.

## Installation

### Downstream packaging status

For detailed instructions for each platform, see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md).

  

### Download a prebuilt binary

We offer several generic binaries in [releases](https://github.com/imsnif/bandwhich/releases) for various OSes.

        All modern Android devices.
        Note that this is a pure binary file, not an APK suitable for general usage.

## Building from source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/imsnif/bandwhich.git
cd bandwhich
cargo build --release
```

For the up-to-date minimum supported Rust version, please refer to the `rust-version` field in [Cargo.toml](Cargo.toml).

### Cross-compiling

Cross-compiling for alternate targets is supported via [cross](https://github.com/cross-rs/cross). Here's the rough procedure:

1. Check the target architecture. If on Linux, you can use `uname -m`.
2. Lookup [rustc platform support](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support.html) for the corresponding target triple.
3. [Install `cross`](https://github.com/cross-rs/cross#installation).
4. Run `cross build --release --target `.

#### Android

Until [cross-rs/cross#1222](https://github.com/cross-rs/cross/issues/1222) is solved, use the latest HEAD:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/cross-rs/cross.git cross
cross build --release --target aarch64-linux-android
```

## Post install (Linux)

Since `bandwhich` sniffs network packets, it requires elevated privileges.
On Linux, there are two main ways to accomplish this:

### 1. `setcap`

- Permanently allow the `bandwhich` binary its required privileges (called "capabilities" in Linux).
- Do this if you want to give all unprivileged users full access to bandwhich's monitoring capabilities.
    - This is the **recommended** setup **for single user machines**, or **if all users are trusted**.
    - This is **not recommended** if you want to **ensure users cannot see others' traffic**.

```sh
# assign capabilities
sudo setcap cap_sys_ptrace,cap_dac_read_search,cap_net_raw,cap_net_admin+ep $(command -v bandwhich)
# run as unprivileged user
bandwhich
```

#### Capabilities explained
- `cap_sys_ptrace,cap_dac_read_search`: allow access to `/proc//fd/`, so that `bandwhich` can determine which open port belongs to which process.
- `cap_net_raw,cap_net_admin`: allow capturing packets on your system.

### 2. `sudo` (or alternative)

- Require privilege escalation every time.
- Do this if you are an administrator of a multi-user environment.

```sh
sudo bandwhich
```

Verdicts

Loopback ports show -: the firewall does not matter for them.

What each system reports
Linux
ufw rules (for given ports or every port, from anywhere or some sources) and default policy; firewalld's default zone (ports, services, target); an empty nftables ruleset means no firewall
portop is not root (the tools refuse), or nftables input rules or firewalld rich rules apply
macOS
The application firewall's global state
It is on but not blocking everything, since it decides per application
Windows
Windows Firewall profiles
Any active profile is on, since rules are per program and slow to enumerate

Rules are read at most every 30 seconds. Turn the check off with --no-firewall or resolve_firewall: false.

Containers and workers

portop names the container behind a port and tells a server's master process from its workers.

Docker and Podman

On Linux the container ID comes from the process's cgroup and the name from the Engine API. The socket is found the way the docker CLI finds it: a unix:// DOCKER_HOST, /var/run/docker.sock, rootless Docker in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, Docker Desktop's ~/.docker/run/docker.sock, then Podman's /run/podman/podman.sock and its rootless socket.

Kubernetes

On a node running containerd or CRI-O, a pod's process is shown as namespace/pod/container. The names come from the kubelet's log links in /var/log/containers, so no API access or crictl is needed; run portop on the node, usually with sudo.

Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows

Containers run inside a VM, so their processes are not visible to the host. portop recognises them by the host ports Docker publishes, which labels the listening rows.

Masters and workers

Pre-forking servers such as nginx, gunicorn, php-fpm and Apache share one listening socket between a master and its workers. portop shows one row owned by the master, the process whose parent does not hold the socket, and counts the others: nginx +3. The details list the workers' PIDs and JSON has a workers array. With socket activation, systemd (PID 1) also holds the socket and is skipped in favour of the service. On Windows a socket has a single owner.

Web dashboard

The same live view in a browser, with process details and confirmed SIGTERM and SIGKILL.

Start
portop --web                  # http://127.0.0.1:8088
portop --web --web-port 9090

The dashboard lists every socket with its exposure and firewall badges, user, workers and traffic, with tabs for listening and connected sockets and a search box. The printed URL carries a per-run token: without it the table is readable, but process details and signals are refused. --listen, the --no-* flags and a filter apply here too.

The web dashboard with a process's details open.
Sign-in
--web-auth
Require sign-in; without a password, one is generated and printed
--web-user NAME
Username (default portop); implies --web-auth
PORTOP_WEB_PASSWORD
Password from the environment
--web-password PASS
Password on the command line, visible to other local users in ps

Sessions last 12 hours and end when portop stops. After five failed sign-ins a client, an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64, waits a minute. Process actions also need a per-session token, so another site cannot use a signed-in cookie.

Remote access and TLS

Only a dashboard with sign-in may listen beyond loopback:

openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -nodes -days 365 \
  -subj "/CN=$(hostname)" -keyout portop.key -out portop.crt
PORTOP_WEB_PASSWORD='choose-one' portop --web --web-user admin \
  --web-addr 0.0.0.0:8088 --web-tls-cert portop.crt --web-tls-key portop.key

Without TLS the password crosses the network unencrypted; portop warns about it. An SSH tunnel to a loopback dashboard needs no certificate: ssh -L 8088:127.0.0.1:8088 host.

Prometheus metrics

/metrics serves the Prometheus text format:

portop_sockets
protocol, state
portop_listening_ports
protocol, scope
portop_listening_port_info
protocol, port, address, scope, firewall, process, pid, user, container (value always 1)
portop_scrape_duration_seconds

With sign-in enabled, /metrics accepts the dashboard credentials as HTTP Basic auth:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: portop
    scheme: https
    basic_auth:
      username: admin
      password: choose-one
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["host:8088"]

Alert when portop_listening_ports{scope="all"} grows, or on a new portop_listening_port_info series.

Baseline drift

Record which ports a host is supposed to listen on, then let a timer tell you when that changes.

Usage
portop --save-baseline     # record what listens now
portop --diff              # exit 3 if anything changed
portop --diff --json       # the same, for scripts

The baseline is a small JSON file in the OS config directory; --baseline-path chooses another.

What is compared

Each listening TCP and UDP port is recorded with its scope: loopback, every interface or one address. A service listening on IPv4 and IPv6 is one entry. --diff reports:

ports listening now that were not in the baseline;
ports in the baseline that no longer listen;
ports whose scope changed, for example a database moving from 127.0.0.1 to 0.0.0.0.

Baselines saved by versions before 0.3.0 have no scope and are compared by protocol and port only.

Run it from a systemd timer
# /etc/systemd/system/portop-diff.service
[Unit]
Description=Compare listening ports with the baseline

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/portop --diff --baseline-path /var/lib/portop/baseline.json

# /etc/systemd/system/portop-diff.timer
[Timer]
OnCalendar=hourly

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

A failed run (exit 3) shows up in systemctl --failed and can trigger OnFailure= alerting.
